svg.aria-label: Diagram: the Google payments profile at Google level above Cloud Billing accounts and subaccounts at cloud level, with the projects they pay for below, and the country and currency fixed at creation
svg.title: Where money attaches in Google Cloud: the payments profile, the billing account, the subaccount and the project
svg.text: Two planes, two consoles, one bill
The payments profile is a Google-level object. The billing account is a Cloud-level one. Only the lower half is in the resource hierarchy.
Google level · managed in the Google payments center
Google payments profile
Country/region, profile type, name, address, tax ID.
One profile pays for Google Ads, Workspace and Fi as well as Cloud.
Type is Individual (only you) or Organization (you can add users).
The country here decides the currency of every account under it.
Cloud level · managed in the Google Cloud console
Cloud Billing account
billingAccounts/{id} · open: true · currencyCode
Ownership is limited to a single organization.
masterBillingAccount is empty: this one is not resold.
A reseller's parent billing account
Billing subaccount — masterBillingAccount names the parent
Its own section of the invoice. The parent pays the charges.
A billing account can be linked to one or more projects, and payment linkage is not limited by organization ownership.
Creating one needs Billing Account Creator on the organization node.
Linking a project needs two grants: Billing Account User on the account, Project Billing Manager on the project.
Projects · where the usage happens
Every cost is tracked against the billing account the project is linked to, across Cloud, Maps, Firebase and AI Studio.
Disable billing and services stop; some resources might be removed and become non-recoverable.
Chosen once, at creation
Country and currency come from the payments profile and cannot be changed later. Editing the country means a new billing account.
